rules.title: Decisions live in one layer
Parse at the boundary, trust inside
Expected failures are values, mapped once
State is explicit, closed, and exhaustive
A unit of work is all-or-nothing
Pay for ceremony only where you collect
Machines enforce, prose explains
Build what is used, delete what is not
One way to do each thing
Wire dependencies at the edge
Tests prove behavior at boundaries, including failure
Ship in small reversible steps and verify at the edge
Secure by construction
The host project wins
Organize the backend as vertical slices, one directory per capability
rules.check: Does every new capability live in its own slice directory with domains, service, transport and tests?

rules.title: Dependencies point inward: transport to service to persistence
rules.check: Do domain modules import zero model or ORM symbols at runtime, and does no module import from a transport module?

rules.title: Name shared code and product code honestly
rules.check: Is every module under a shared/common package free of product-specific nouns and rules?

rules.title: No speculative modules: every slice has a caller and a test
rules.check: Does every new module have at least one caller outside itself and at least one test?

rules.title: Every slice documents its service API in a short README
rules.check: If a service method or endpoint changed, did the slice README change in the same diff?

rules.title: Parse every request into a request domain at the transport boundary
rules.check: Does every handler obtain all of its inputs from a single parsed request domain?

rules.title: Request domains are strict about types and lenient about extras
rules.check: Does each request field have the narrowest type that fits, and are unknown fields ignored rather than rejected?

rules.title: Validate strictly on input, serialize leniently on output
rules.check: Can every row already in the database be serialized by the response domain without raising?

rules.title: Define each vocabulary once as an enum and branch on its members
rules.check: Is every fixed vocabulary declared once and compared by member everywhere?

rules.title: Domain objects are plain values: no queries, no I/O
rules.check: Can every domain class be constructed in a unit test with no database and no network?

rules.title: Business rules live in services; transport never touches persistence
rules.check: Is the handler free of ORM calls and of branching on business conditions?

rules.title: Inject collaborators through the constructor; wire defaults in a factory
rules.check: Does the service obtain every collaborator from its constructor rather than importing and instantiating it inline?

rules.title: Cross-slice access goes through the other slice's service
rules.check: Does each service touch only its own slice's models?

rules.title: Services take and return domain values, never ORM objects
rules.check: Do service signatures mention only primitives and domain types?

rules.title: Raise typed business errors from one exception hierarchy
rules.check: Does every expected failure raised by a service derive from the shared business-error base?

rules.title: Make retried writes idempotent
rules.check: Is there a test that performs the write twice and asserts no duplicate?

rules.title: Compute derived state in one pure helper shared by reads and writes
rules.check: Is each derivation implemented exactly once?

rules.title: One service method is one transaction
rules.check: Does every multi-write service method run in one transaction, with a test that forces a late failure and asserts nothing persisted?

rules.title: Never hold a transaction open across an outbound network call
rules.check: Is every remote call outside all transaction blocks?

rules.title: Recover from an integrity error only inside a savepoint
rules.check: Is every caught integrity error raised from inside a nested atomic block?

rules.title: Run irreversible side effects after commit
rules.check: Are all non-database side effects registered to run on commit?

rules.title: A handler authenticates, parses, calls one service method, and responds
rules.check: Does the handler consist only of parse, one service call and the response?

rules.title: One error contract for the whole API, produced in one place
rules.check: Does every error path, including validation and malformed input, produce the single error shape with a 4xx status?

rules.title: Write error messages for the end user; clients show them verbatim
rules.check: Would every error message make sense to a person who has never seen the code?

rules.title: Never echo upstream or configuration detail to callers; log it instead
rules.check: Can any response body contain text produced by a third party or by a configuration check?

rules.title: Deny by default: endpoints are authenticated unless they opt out
rules.check: Is every public endpoint public through the explicit opt-out base and nothing else?

rules.title: Scope every lookup to the caller; foreign and unknown IDs look the same
rules.check: For every client-supplied ID, is there a test using another tenant's ID that gets 404?

rules.title: Cap everything the client controls
rules.check: Does every client-controlled size or option have a tested limit?

rules.title: Timestamps cross the boundary as ISO-8601 with an offset
rules.check: Is every timestamp field on a request domain timezone-aware?

rules.title: Reserve 401 for dead credentials
rules.check: Can any non-credential failure produce a 401?

rules.title: Liveness is shallow and dependency-free; readiness checks dependencies
rules.check: Does the liveness handler run zero queries, and does something else monitor the dependencies?

rules.title: Third-party credentials stay server-side behind an allowlisting proxy
rules.check: Is the upstream request built field by field from an allowlist, with redirects disabled and a timeout?

rules.title: Wrap each provider SDK in one adapter with its own error types
rules.check: Is the provider SDK imported in exactly one module?

rules.title: Application code reads configuration from the environment only
rules.check: Does application code import any cloud SDK to read configuration?

rules.title: Generate migrations from models; never hand-write or edit them
rules.check: Does CI fail when models and migrations disagree, and is every migration file tool-generated?

rules.title: Use opaque, non-sequential identifiers and audit timestamps
rules.check: Do new tables inherit the shared base model?

rules.title: Enforce uniqueness in the database and handle the conflict in code
rules.check: Is every uniqueness rule backed by a constraint and a tested conflict path?

rules.title: Select the settings profile with one switch
rules.check: Is there exactly one mechanism that selects the profile?

rules.title: Production configuration validates itself and refuses to boot when unsafe
rules.check: Does booting production with an unsafe value fail, and does CI run the production configuration check?

rules.title: No secret in any repository or client; one store, one manifest, one test
rules.check: Does a test fail if a setting is read that the manifest does not declare?

rules.title: Trust a proxy header only after verifying it arrives at the origin
rules.check: Is each trusted header backed by evidence captured at the origin?

rules.title: Organize the client by experience; each owns its flow end to end
rules.check: Does each feature's code live under one experience directory with the six sub-folders it needs?

rules.title: Dependencies point inward: presentation, manager, services, models
rules.check: Does any model import a service or storage module, or any component import a service?

rules.title: Share code only after a second real use
rules.check: Does everything in the shared area have at least two callers or is it single-by-nature infrastructure?

rules.title: Routes are composition roots: build services once, inject, decide nothing
rules.check: Does the route construct each service exactly once per mount and contain no conditional workflow?

rules.title: Intents are explicit events in a closed, tagged union
rules.check: Is every event a member of one tagged union with a literal `kind`?

rules.title: Renderable states are explicit, tagged, and shaped for the UI
rules.check: Does presentation select what to render by `state.kind` with no `instanceof` chains or optional-field probing?

rules.title: Dispatch exhaustively; an unknown event is an error
rules.check: Does adding a new event type without a case fail the type check?

rules.title: Give orthogonal concerns separate state machines
rules.check: Does any single state union mix two concerns that can change independently?

rules.title: Background work is sub-state of the loaded state, never a replacement
rules.check: Does the manager hold any variable that duplicates data from a previous state?

rules.title: A submission owns the flow until it settles
rules.check: Is there a test showing that a result arriving during a submission leaves the state `Submitting`?

rules.title: Never show data loaded for a different key
rules.check: Is there a test that switches keys and asserts the loading state is empty?

rules.title: State carries data and intent; presentation owns the words
rules.check: Does any manager state contain a user-facing sentence, or any component branch on one?

rules.title: Derive view models with pure functions
rules.check: Is each derived display value computed in one tested pure function?

rules.title: The manager is a plain class; the framework binding is a thin adapter
rules.check: Can the manager be constructed and driven in a unit test with no UI framework import?

rules.title: The manager owns sequencing, branching, validation, and automatic actions
rules.check: Is there any conditional about the workflow outside the manager and its pure helpers?

rules.title: Compute each transition from the state at the moment the result arrives
rules.check: Does every post-await transition read the current state inside the update function?

rules.title: Resolve flags and environment at the composition root and pass them in
rules.check: Does any file outside routes and the flag model read the environment?

rules.title: Forms report snapshots; validity and submission mapping are pure functions
rules.check: Are validity and request mapping pure functions with tests, not code in a component?

rules.title: Every service method returns a result value: failure left, success right
rules.check: Does every service method's return type include the failure arm, with no expected failure thrown?

rules.title: Normalize failures at the service boundary into typed codes
rules.check: Does the manager branch on failure codes only, never on message text?

rules.title: Show users only messages your own API wrote
rules.check: Can a browser or parser error string reach the UI?

rules.title: One HTTP client owns URLs, headers, error parsing, and auth
rules.check: Is `fetch` (or the HTTP library) called from exactly one module?

rules.title: Refresh once on 401; clear tokens only when the session is provably dead
rules.check: Do tests prove a 5xx or network error during refresh leaves both tokens in place?

rules.title: Storage keys live in one module and storage is injected
rules.check: Does each key string appear in exactly one source file?

rules.title: Map wire formats to models in one place at the service boundary
rules.check: Does any code outside a service or mapper reference a wire field name?

rules.title: Keep concurrency guards on instances and make effects idempotent
rules.check: Is there any mutable module-level variable in a service?

rules.title: Nothing in the bundle is secret; build-time configuration needs a rebuild
rules.check: Does any client environment variable hold a secret?

rules.title: Components render state and emit events; local state is ephemeral only
rules.check: Does any component hold state that outlives the interaction or affects the workflow?

rules.title: No services, storage, environment, or business branching in presentation
rules.check: Do presentation files import any service, storage helper or environment accessor?

rules.title: Business constants and rules are pure, tested model functions
rules.check: Does any component define a constant or predicate with business meaning?

rules.title: Test hooks in the markup are a contract; refactors keep them
rules.check: Are all selectors used by end-to-end tests still present after the change?

rules.title: Consume design tokens and shared primitives; never duplicate them
rules.check: Does the change hard-code a value that exists as a token or re-create an existing primitive?

rules.title: One documented error shape; clients parse only that
rules.check: Do both sides implement the same single error shape?

rules.title: Status codes carry meaning both sides act on
rules.check: Does each failure path return the status this table assigns?

rules.title: Absent and null mean the same; clients omit empty optionals
rules.check: Does each optional field accept both an omitted key and null?

rules.title: The server owns workflow state; the client derives display from it
rules.check: Does the client persist or compute workflow position independently of the server?

rules.title: Every mutation returns the full updated snapshot
rules.check: Does each write endpoint return the same shape as its read endpoint?

rules.title: Read paths tolerate legacy data and unknown fields
rules.check: Is there a test reading a record that contains a retired value?

rules.title: A contract change lands on both sides with tests and a written note
rules.check: Does the change description list every contract change and the client impact of each?

rules.title: State the auth transport and its consequences
rules.check: Is the auth transport documented with its origin policy and token-storage decision?

rules.title: Test at the boundary each layer exposes
rules.check: Does each new behaviour have a test at its layer's public boundary?

rules.title: Prove every fix red before green
rules.check: Does the change state that each new regression test failed before the fix?

rules.title: Failure paths are first-class test cases
rules.check: For each new write path, is there a rollback test and, where a constraint exists, a conflict test?

rules.title: Fakes fail loudly
rules.check: Would the test fail if the code called the collaborator with a wrong argument or one extra time?

rules.title: A test asserts exactly what its name claims
rules.check: Does each test assert every outcome its name states?

rules.title: Tests are deterministic, order-independent, and offline
rules.check: Does the suite pass in shuffled order with the network disabled?

rules.title: Run the same command locally and in CI, and know what it selects
rules.check: Is the CI test step the same command the README documents, and is the engine it selects stated?

rules.title: Exercise transactions and constraints on the production database engine
rules.check: Were the transaction and constraint tests run on the production engine?

rules.title: A pattern justified by testability must have tests
rules.check: Does every manager, derivation and service introduced have tests that CI runs?

rules.title: Keep end-to-end tests few, on stable hooks, with stated prerequisites
rules.check: Are the prerequisites for each end-to-end test written down, including feature-flag values?

rules.title: Contract-test configuration: code, infrastructure, and docs must agree
rules.check: Is each multiply-declared fact covered by a test that compares its sources?

rules.title: CI gates every change: lint, types, tests, deploy checks
rules.check: Does CI run every check the project relies on, including the newly added one?

rules.title: CI has least privilege and pinned dependencies
rules.check: Do check jobs run without cloud credentials and are all actions pinned to a commit?

rules.title: A deploy workflow re-tests before it ships
rules.check: Does the deploy workflow run the test suite on the revision it ships?

rules.title: Gate deploys with an explicit switch checked before credentials
rules.check: Is the gate a job-level condition that runs before credentials are requested?

rules.title: Know what triggers a deploy; baked configuration needs a rebuild
rules.check: After this change merges, is a manual deploy or rebuild needed, and is that written in the change description?

rules.title: Releases are additive until an atomic swap, then health-gated
rules.check: Can every step before the swap fail without affecting traffic, and does a failed health check restore the previous release?

rules.title: Assert the safety net before any irreversible step
rules.check: Is each irreversible step preceded by an assertion of its safety net?

rules.title: Publish hashed assets first, the entry document last and uncached
rules.check: Is the entry document uploaded after its assets and served uncached?

rules.title: Verify a deploy by observing new behavior at the public edge
rules.check: Does the change description record evidence taken from the public endpoint after deploy?

rules.title: Work in a fresh branch from current main, never in a dirty checkout
rules.check: Was the work done in a task-specific branch from current main with no unrelated files touched?

rules.title: Re-fetch and compare before squashing; check for silent removals
rules.check: Does the diff against the current base contain only changes this task intended?

rules.title: Infrastructure applies are deliberate, never automatic from defaults
rules.check: Can CI apply infrastructure without a deliberate human or protected step?

rules.title: A pull request states what, why, contract changes, evidence, and rollback
rules.check: Does the description contain all five parts with concrete evidence?

rules.title: Review through independent lenses
rules.check: Was each lens applied, and is the outcome of each recorded?

rules.title: A finding needs a location, evidence, a failure scenario, and a fix
rules.check: Does every finding include all five parts?

rules.title: Verify a finding before acting on it
rules.check: Is each acted-on finding marked as verified, with how?

rules.title: Re-audit every fix independently
rules.check: Was each finding re-checked against the final diff by someone who did not write the fix?

rules.title: Classify by severity and keep an append-only debt ledger
rules.check: Is every unfixed finding in the ledger with a rule ID and a disposition?

rules.title: Exercise the change in the running product, including flag states
rules.check: Is there a recorded run of the change in the product for each flag state?

rules.title: Merge on green checks, clean review, and passing QA; else a human decides
rules.check: Are all three gates green, or has a person explicitly accepted the remaining findings?

rules.title: Follow the precedence order: user, project, existing code, Doctrine
rules.check: Where the change departs from Doctrine, is the higher-precedence source named?

rules.title: Detect the adoption mode before writing code
rules.check: Is the adoption mode stated at the start of the work?

rules.title: Apply the principle in the local idiom; never plant a competing pattern
rules.check: Does the change use the project's existing mechanisms for layering, errors and state?

rules.title: No drive-by refactors
rules.check: Is every changed line required by the task?

rules.title: When a rule cannot be met, say so and record it as debt with its ID
rules.check: Is each unmet rule named with a reason?

rules.title: Migrate existing code in order of risk removed per unit of effort
rules.check: Does the migration plan start with data integrity and input validation rather than restructuring?
